outputs.L3:
The bearing structure includes a housing provided with a bearing hole in which a bearing is installed to rotatably support a shaft. A clearance groove is formed in the bearing hole and includes an opposing wall portion positioned radially opposite the shaft. The clearance groove communicates with an oil drainage passage located below the center of the shaft, thereby allowing oil to drain from the bearing region.

The opposing wall portion includes at least one narrow portion and one wide portion, with the boundary between these portions positioned directly above the center of the shaft. Relative to the shaft’s direction of rotation, the narrow portion is located behind the boundary and forms a smaller radial gap with the shaft. Conversely, the wide portion is located ahead of the boundary in the rotation direction and forms a larger radial gap with the shaft.
outputs.L4:
A bearing structure includes a housing that supports a bearing around a rotating shaft. The housing is provided with a clearance groove extending around at least part of the shaft and communicating with an oil drainage passage located below the shaft. Lubricating oil discharged from or passing through the bearing enters the clearance groove and is directed by gravity toward the lower oil drainage passage, through which it is removed from the region surrounding the bearing.

The clearance between the shaft and the wall defining the groove is asymmetric with respect to a boundary positioned directly above the center of the shaft. The two sides of this boundary are identified according to the shaft’s direction of rotation: a front side located downstream in the rotation direction and a rear side located upstream in the rotation direction. The wall may be shaped so that the radial gap on the rear side is narrower than the corresponding gap on the front side. Alternatively, or in combination, the front-side gap may be enlarged relative to the rear-side gap.

This asymmetric arrangement controls the movement of oil carried circumferentially by the rotating shaft. The narrower rear-side gap restricts oil from accumulating or flowing backward around the shaft, while the wider front-side gap provides additional space for oil transported in the rotation direction. The oil can therefore move more readily toward the lower portion of the clearance groove and enter the drainage passage.

By promoting discharge of excess oil, the structure reduces oil retention, agitation, and associated frictional losses around the bearing. It can also limit undesirable temperature increases and help maintain a more stable supply and distribution of lubricant. As a result, the bearing structure provides more effective oil drainage and improved lubrication management without requiring a substantially larger housing or a complex auxiliary drainage mechanism.
outputs.L5:
## A Bearing Structure

A bearing structure is the part of a building or construction that supports and transfers loads safely to the ground. It gives the structure stability, strength, and durability. Typical load-bearing elements include foundations, columns, beams, walls, floors, and roof frames.

Loads acting on a structure can be permanent, such as the weight of the building itself, or temporary, such as people, furniture, vehicles, snow, and wind. The bearing structure must distribute these forces without excessive deformation, cracking, or collapse. Its design therefore requires careful calculations and compliance with construction standards.

Common materials used for bearing structures include reinforced concrete, steel, timber, brick, and stone. The choice depends on the building’s purpose, size, location, cost, and environmental conditions. A well-designed bearing structure not only ensures safety but also supports efficient construction and a long service life.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent claim for a bearing structure with a housing, a bearing hole, a shaft-supporting bearing, a clearance groove connected to a lower oil drainage passage, and an asymmetric groove gap based on the shaft’s rotation direction.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an oil-draining bearing structure in formal patent language, specifying narrow and wide portions of a clearance groove on opposite sides of a boundary directly above the shaft center.
counterfactuals.output:
An oil-draining bearing structure comprising:

a bearing body rotatably supporting a shaft and having an inner circumferential surface opposed to an outer circumferential surface of the shaft; and

a clearance groove formed in the inner circumferential surface of the bearing body and configured to discharge lubricating oil from a clearance between the bearing body and the shaft,

wherein an imaginary radial line extending vertically upward from a center axis of the shaft defines a boundary within the clearance groove,

wherein the clearance groove includes a narrow portion disposed on a first circumferential side of the boundary and a wide portion disposed on a second circumferential side of the boundary opposite the first circumferential side, and

wherein the wide portion has a groove width greater than a groove width of the narrow portion.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a single independent apparatus claim for a housing-mounted bearing that reduces oil accumulation by making the rear side of a clearance groove narrower than the front side relative to shaft rotation.
counterfactuals.output: 1. A bearing apparatus comprising: a housing; a shaft rotatably supported in the housing and having a predetermined rotational direction; and a bearing mounted in the housing and surrounding the shaft, the bearing having an inner circumferential surface defining a clearance groove including a front-side portion and a rear-side portion arranged relative to the predetermined rotational direction of the shaft, wherein the rear-side portion has a smaller width than the front-side portion to reduce accumulation of oil in the clearance groove.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention concept into patent-claim style: a shaft is pivotally supported in a bearing hole, the hole has a clearance groove communicating with an oil drain below the shaft center, and the groove-to-shaft spacing varies circumferentially according to the direction of rotation.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **A bearing structure comprising:**

a shaft configured to rotate in a predetermined rotational direction;

a bearing portion having a bearing hole in which the shaft is pivotally supported; and

a clearance groove formed in an inner circumferential surface of the bearing hole and communicating with an oil drain disposed below a center axis of the shaft,

wherein a radial spacing between the clearance groove and an outer circumferential surface of the shaft varies in a circumferential direction in relation to the predetermined rotational direction of the shaft.
